By general consent, it wan Sir William xfarcourt,who, in the character of Lord !Chancellor Harcourt, otood literally head aid !shoulders over all his fellows, and showed a dignity of bearing which fairly put his rivals, younger sod elder, in the shade. Lord Rosebery's appearance At the National Liberal Club on Saturday was in striking contrast to his previous appearance at that institution. On that last occasion he was indisposed, and his I speech lacked the epigrammatic brightnere that usually marks his utterances. On Saturday he was in admirable health, and his epeech was charec• terised by a bright buoyancy of phrase and His voice seems to have improved in tone by ab- stention from public oratory, and its rhythmic note was admirably attuned to hie epigrams. The club- men were delighted, and Sir William Harcourt joined cordially in their applause.

Sir William himmlf spoke with an evident manse I ,of responsibility. It was only on two or three oc- casions that the statesman indulged in his lighter vein. The Colonists had him in his most dignill,d mood—the mood of sonorous phrase, deep-bard utterance, and careful dramatic emphasis. Fir Wilfrid Laurier listened to Sir William with deep illumine.. The speech elicited many cheeru from the democratic Mr. Seddon.

. On Friday morning lest a young man named James Millard, living at the Vitriol, Harlentown, had a marvellous escape from drowning. It appeara Millard in employed at the Vulcan Foundry, and on Friday morning about nix o'clock, being ratner late, he rode his bicycle at • good speed along the lowing path of the London and N 001-Western Rsilvray Co.'s canal. On the way the Dent wheel of the machine rum, in contact with a brick, and unfortunately the hendle bar lick,' , there being an arrangement by w'rich LIIP bar c -mid he locked, and , the coneequence was he was thrown headlong into the middle of the canal.
